title: Locating Places on the Earth — Class 6 CBSE Social Science
subject: Social Science

slides.title: Locating Places on the Earth
slides.speaker_notes: How do we find ANY place on Earth precisely? With a grid of imaginary lines.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Compare a globe and a map.
Name the major parallels and meridians.
Compute time differences using the 15° rule.

slides.title: Shape of the Earth
bullets: Earth is an OBLATE SPHEROID — slightly flattened sphere.
Bulged at the equator; flattened at the poles.
Spinning axis: ends at the NORTH and SOUTH poles.
From space, looks like a blue-green ball.

slides.title: Globe vs Map
bullets: GLOBE: round; accurate; hard to carry.
MAP: flat; easy to carry; shows detail; distorts shapes.
Both are useful — they complement each other.

slides.title: Latitudes (parallels)
bullets: East-west lines, parallel to the equator.
Arctic Circle = 66½° N; Antarctic Circle = 66½° S.

slides.title: Heat zones
bullets: Torrid Zone — between the two tropics. HOT.
Temperate Zones — tropics to polar circles. MILD.
Frigid Zones — inside polar circles. VERY COLD.
India is mostly in the Torrid Zone.

slides.title: Longitudes (meridians)
bullets: Measured 0° to 180° east AND 0° to 180° west.
All meridians are the SAME length.

slides.title: Hemispheres
bullets: Eastern hemisphere — east of the Prime Meridian.
Western hemisphere — west of the Prime Meridian.
Each place is in TWO hemispheres.

slides.title: Coordinates — finding a place
bullets: Use N/S for lat; E/W for long.

slides.title: Find (28.6° N, 77.2° E)
bullets: Step 3: where they cross — that's the place.

slides.title: Time and the 15° rule
bullets: Each 15° of longitude = 1 hour of time difference.
East is AHEAD; west is BEHIND.

slides.title: Greenwich → India (75° E)
bullets: India is 5 h AHEAD of Greenwich.
(IST is set to 82.5° E, so actual difference is 5 h 30 min.)

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Latitudes (parallels) measure N/S; longitudes (meridians) measure E/W.
Equator (0° lat) and Prime Meridian (0° long) are the master references.
